subject: SLA template — uptime target & exception request
messages:
From: Samantha Holt <samantha.holt@nimbus-pay.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nimbus Contracts <contracts@nimbus-pay.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood SLA draft — uptime threshold question

Marcus — thanks for sending over the draft SLA. Our legal and ops teams reviewed it and have one substantive ask before we can finalize: can Redwood commit to a 99.95% monthly uptime (vs. the 99.9% listed in the doc) for the production inference endpoint used by our payments tokenization flow?

The reason: our payments latency/availability directly impacts settlement SLAs with our processor; even short, frequent blips create reconciliations downstream. If Redwood can't increase the uptime target, Nimbus needs a materially larger monthly service credit for outages between 99.9% and 99.95% (we'd propose a pro-rata credit equal to 25% of monthly fees for >2 hours total downtime).

Per process, I'm including our contracts team on cc (contracts@nimbus-pay.com). Attached is the SOW and our initial comments. Happy to jump on a short call if easier.

—Sam
Samantha Holt
Head of Platform Operations, Nimbus Payments
S: +1 415-555-0123

Attachment: Nimbus_SOW.pdf (pdf)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Holt <samantha.holt@nimbus-pay.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood SLA draft — uptime threshold question

Sam — thanks for the clear note and for attaching the SOW. Appreciate why Nimbus is asking for 99.95%. A few immediate datapoints from our side: our standard enterprise SLA for hosted inference is 99.9% monthly uptime with service credits that scale (up to 50% of monthly fees in extreme cases). We measure uptime at the model endpoint level (health-check + successful token delivery) and exclude scheduled maintenance windows (we propose 4h/month, notified 72h in advance).

That said, we are open to an exception conversation for mission-critical flows like payments. Operationally a 99.95% target implies more aggressive capacity reservation and cross-region active fallback which changes economics. Before we do that, two asks so we can get legal and infra aligned:

- Laura, can you confirm whether we have precedent for a 99.95% commit (and what the credit structure looked like)?
- Evelyn, can the infra team scope the additional run-rate/capacity required to meet 99.95% for a single customer endpoint (rough estimate)?

Sam — if agreeable, we can propose a compromise: 99.95% as a pilot commitment for the first 3 months after go-live with an elevated credit of 25% of monthly fees for the band between 99.9%–99.95% (capped at 25% of invoice), followed by a performance review and adjustments. For unplanned downtime above that band we'd follow the standard credit tables in the attached SLA_Redwood_v2.docx. Also propose a joint runbook and a canary/failover window during cutover.

If that sounds reasonable, I'll ask legal to circulate a redline. Otherwise happy to hop on a 30-min call tomorrow.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Account Exec — Strategic Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA_Redwood_v2.docx (docx)

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Samantha Holt <samantha.holt@nimbus-pay.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood SLA draft — uptime threshold question

Marcus / Sam — quick legal view and proposed redlines attached. High-level positions:

- We can agree to a customer-specific 99.95% commitment for the production inference endpoint as a time-boxed exception (recommended: 3 months) provided we:
  * Limit the exception to the named endpoint(s) in the SOW;
  * Exclude force majeure and customer-caused network issues;
  * Cap incremental credits for that band at 25% of the monthly invoice for the pilot period;
  * Require a post-pilot review and written amendment for longer-term commitments.

- We are not comfortable with an open-ended 25% credit for every month without performance telemetry and a capacity plan. Suggest we require SLO telemetry (95th/99th latencies, error rates) and a joint incident review process.

Redlines (redlines_legal.docx) include: clarification on measurement method, clear exclusion list, and a maximum aggregate credit cap for month = 50% of monthly fees (matching enterprise policy) with the pilot band capped at 25%. Also added a rollback clause if the pilot materially affects other customers' latency.

If Nimbus accepts the pilot terms, Laura to circulate final redline for signature and Marcus to confirm infra estimate.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Holt <samantha.holt@nimbus-pay.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nimbus Contracts <contracts@nimbus-pay.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 15:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Redwood SLA draft — uptime threshold question

Marcus / Laura / Evelyn — thanks for the quick turnaround and the proposed compromise. Nimbus is comfortable with the pilot approach as long as two items are explicit in the redline:

1) 99.95% monthly uptime for the named production inference endpoint for an initial 3-month pilot starting on go-live date;
2) A floor credit schedule: if monthly uptime falls between 99.9%–99.95% we receive a pro-rata credit equal to 15% of monthly fees (we concede to 15% for the pilot; we requested 25% originally).

We understand exclusions for maintenance and force majeure. We also agree to the performance review and telemetry requirement — we'll provide our side's monitoring hooks and accept a joint incident review cadence.

If you can circulate the redline with those two bullet points (pilot length & the 15% pilot-band credit) we can move to signatures. Contracts will route the DocuSign once legal confirms the language.

Best,
Sam
Samantha Holt
Head of Platform Operations, Nimbus Payments

Attachment: acceptance_note.txt (text)
